==English==
{{wp|we<dab!>}}

===Etymology 1===
{{etymon|en|id=nominative|:inh|enm:we<id:pronoun>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|we}}, from {{inh|en|ang|wē||we}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*wiʀ}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*wīz}}, {{m|ine-pro|*wiz||we}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*wéy||we (plural)}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|wee}}, {{m|sco|we||we}}, {{cog|frr|we||we}}, {{cog|fy|wy||we}}, {{cog|nds|wi||we}}, {{cog|nl|we}}, {{m|nl|wij||we}}, {{cog|de|wir||we}}, {{cog|da|-}}, {{cog|sv|-}} and {{cog|no|vi||we}}, {{cog|is|vér}}, {{m|is|við||we}}, {{cog|ae|𐬬𐬀𐬉𐬨}}, {{cog|sa|वयम्|tr=vayám}}.

====Pronunciation====
* {{enPR|wē|a=RP,CA}}, {{IPA|en|/wiː/}}
* {{audio|en|En-uk-we.ogg|a=UK}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Greenman-we.wav}}
* {{IPA|en|/wi/|a=GA}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-we.ogg|a=US}}
* {{homophones|en|oui|wee|Wii|;|whee|aa3=wine-whine}}
* {{rhymes|en|iː|s=1}}

====Pronoun====
{{en-pron|desc=first-person plural [[personal pronoun]] nominative case|objective case|us|possessive determiner|our|possessive pronoun|ours|reflexive|ourselves|reflexive singular|ourself}}

# Two or more people including or consisting of the speaker(s)/writer(s).
## {{senseid|en|exclusive we}} Excluding the person(s) being addressed. {{qualifier|This is the [[exclusive]] ''we''.}}
##: {{ux|en|'''We''' are here to arrest you.}}
##* {{RQ:Guardian
|date=February 20, 2017
|author=Paul Mason
|title=Climate scepticism is a far-right badge of honour – even in sweltering Australia
|url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2017/feb/20/sweltering-aussies-rightwing-climate-of-fear
|passage= It’s time to overcome queasiness and restraint. '''We''', the liberal and progressive people of the world, are at war with the far right to save the earth.|archiveurl=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/wCdbM|archivedate=31 August 2025}}
## {{senseid|en|inclusive we}} Including the person(s) being addressed. {{qualifier|This is the [[inclusive]] ''we''.}}
##: {{ux|en|'''We''' need to have a talk, you and me.}}
# {{senseid|en|editorial we}} The institution which the speaker/writer is acting for. {{qualifier|This is the [[editorial we|editorial ''we'']], used by writers and others when speaking with the authority of their publication or organisation.}}
#: {{ux|en|'''We''' will in due course state our reasons for publishing the name of the accused.}}
#: {{ux|en|As the government, '''we''' have a duty to ensure public safety.}}
# Any other entity that the speaker is a part of or identifies with, such as place of employment or education, [[nation]], [[region]], [[language]], etc.
#: {{ux|en|I went to watch our school football match against Puddletown High. '''We''' lost 2-0.}}
#: {{ux|en|In English, '''we''' do not inflect adjectives for gender.}}
# {{senseid|en|people in general}} People in general.
#: {{ux|en|'''We''' live and learn.}}
#: {{ux|en|'''We''' still have much to learn about quantum mechanics.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=2013|month=July-August|author=[http://www.americanscientist.org/authors/detail/stephen-p-lownie Stephen P. Lownie]; [http://www.americanscientist.org/authors/detail/david-m-pelz David M. Pelz]
|magazine=w:American Scientist|title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/feature/2013/4/stents-to-prevent-stroke Stents to Prevent Stroke]
|passage=As '''we''' age, the major arteries of our bodies frequently become thickened with plaque, a fatty material with an oatmeal-like consistency that builds up along the inner lining of blood vessels.}}
# {{senseid|en|royal we}} {{lb|en|royal}} The [[sovereign]] alone in his or her capacity as [[monarch]]. {{qualifier|This is the [[royal we|royal ''we'']]. The reflexive case of this sense of ''we'' is ''[[ourself]]''.}}
#: {{ux|en|'''We''' are Queen of all these Isles.}}
# {{lb|en|colloquial}} Everyone being addressed.
#: {{ux|en|Good evening everyone. How are '''we''' all tonight?}}
# {{senseid|en|nurse_s we, doctor_s we}} {{lb|en|colloquial|;|may sometimes seem patronising}} An individual being addressed; {{n-g|used especially to a person in the speaker's care, or to whom advice or instruction is being given.}} {{qualifier|Sometimes called the [[nurse's we|nurse's ''we'']] or the [[doctor's we|doctor's ''we'']].}}
#: {{ux|en|Hello Mrs Miggins. How are '''we''' feeling this morning?}}
#: {{ux|en|You've been spending all your money boozing when you have a spouse and family to support. I think '''we''' need to get our priorities straight.}}
#* {{RQ:Dickens Sketches by Boz|volume=I|title=The Boarding-House|chapter=II|page=204|passage=“Well, my dear ma’am, and how are '''we'''?” inquired Wosky in a soothing tone. / “Very ill, doctor—very ill,” said Mrs. Bloss in a whisper.}}
# {{lb|en|colloquial|uncommon}} {{n-g|Used to refer to a third person, especially someone in the speaker's care.}}
#: {{ux|en|"I've just been to see Mrs Miggins." — "And how is she?" — "I'm afraid '''we''' aren't too good today."}}
# {{n-g|Used to connect to or include readers or listeners.}}
## {{lb|en|colloquial<!--as in "restricted to speech"-->}} {{n-g|Used to imply connection between the speaker's experiences or activities and a group of listeners}}. {{qualifier|Compare the [[plural of modesty]].}}
##: {{ux|en|Hey guys, in this video I'll show you how I make my upside-down sponge cake. First '''we''' take 200{{nbsp}}g of butter and '''we''' whisk in 200{{nbsp}}g of sugar. Next, '''we''' ...}}
##* {{quote-av|en|title=Alone|text=[Today is] not a day to think about fishing so '''we''' will get back to working on the shelter. [cut in video] Cool, so I guess the best analogy for this, then, is that '''we''''ve basically framed the house, and now '''we''' get to shingle.|date=2021-06-24|role=Theresa Emmerich Kamper|medium=televison production|time=3:07|network=HISTORY Channel|season=9|number=4|episode=Far from Home|url=https://play.history.com/shows/alone/season-8/episode-4}}
## {{n-g|Used in explanatory or procedural writing, such as mathematical explanations, to imply inclusion of the reader in the undertaking.}}
##: {{ux|en|To solve the equation, '''we''' first collect all the terms in ''x'' on one side.}}
# {{lb|en|colloquial<!--as in "restricted to speech"-->}} {{n-g|Used when talking to oneself to refer to oneself.}}
#: {{ux|en|Now then ... let me see ... I hope I'm doing this right ... if '''we''' just connect these two wires together ...}}
# {{lb|en|West Country|archaic}} [[us|Us]].
# {{lb|en|bridge}} The side which is [[keep score|keeping score]].
#: {{ant|en|they}}

====Determiner====
{{en-head|det}}

# {{n-g|Designates the speaker(s)/writer(s) as belonging to or constituting the stated category of people.}}
#: {{ux|en|'''We''' Canadians like to think of ourselves as different.}}
#: {{ux|en|'''We''' the undersigned wish to express our disapproval.}}

===Etymology 2===
{{etymon|en|id=us|:from<text:case extension of>|we<id:nominative>}}
Case extension of nominative {{m|en|we}}, used in the objective case in Tyneside English.

====Pronunciation====
* {{IPA|en|/wə/}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-we2.wav|a=Southern England}}

====Pronoun====
{{en-pron}}

# {{senseid|en|us}}{{lb|en|Tyneside}} [[us|Us]].
#: {{ux|en|He was a propa gadgie, and always bought '''we''' drinks after a long shift.|t=He was a great guy, and always bought '''us''' drinks after a long shift.}}
#: {{ux|en|And what have you done for '''we''' since? Nowt!|t=And what have you done for '''us''' since? Nothing!}}

=====Usage notes=====
Not to be confused with Tyneside {{m|en|us||me}}.
